html:
SMTO-TSK-0003 — This task or conversation changed before your action went through

GUID: 0f0ab183-195c-4b55-b84d-e5f3b0700d20
Slug: task-lane-conflict
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • Something in this conversation changed after you started your action. For example, a task finished, a setting changed or new work arrived. SMTO didn't apply your action so it wouldn't act on outdated information.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page so you see the conversation's current tasks and status. Your screen may be showing an older state than the one SMTO has saved.
  2. If you were deleting conversations, select Delete conversation again, review the updated list, and confirm discarding any queued prompts if asked. SMTO only deletes after you've reviewed the latest list, including queued prompts that never started.
  3. If you were steering a running task, check that it's still running; if it has finished, send your message as a new request instead. You can only steer a task that is still running with the same settings.
  4. If a task is still running or waiting in this conversation, let it finish or stop it before trying again. Some actions, like deleting a conversation, are blocked while its work is unfinished.

What success looks like

  • Your action goes through and the conversation shows the expected result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, noting what you were trying to do. Don't abandon work that's still running just to get past this message.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A task-lane, admission, steering or conversation-management check found that the current state differs from what the action expected (ownership, policy snapshot, selection or safety digest, missing work, or unconfirmed deletion choices).

What this means

  • A lane, admission, steering or management check found incompatible current ownership, policy/snapshot, selection/safety digest, missing work or unconfirmed deletion choices. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A lane, admission, steering or management check found incompatible current ownership, policy/snapshot, selection/safety digest, missing work or unconfirmed deletion choices.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific conflict code and current lane or deletion preview; this shared kind does not prove another client changed a revision.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the current lane and task snapshot or the conversation-management preview (selection_digest, safety_digest, blockers, queued tasks) and resubmit with current values; the LaneConflict or ManagementConflict message names the specific conflict. Do not resubmit stale identifiers or revisions, and resolve unfinished runs before deleting a conversation.
  • Refresh the relevant lane or management preview and correct its specific conflict without replacing accepted work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended action matches current ownership, reviewed state and required explicit choices.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
